records.source: הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וַאֲדַבֵּ֑רָה וְתִשְׁמַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ אִמְרֵי־פִֽי׃
records.gloss: Give ear, the heavens, and let me speak; and let hear the earth [the] words of my mouth.
pieces: "Listen, heavens, and I will speak; \q earth, hear the words I say.

L.1: "Give ear, heavens, and let me speak; \q and let the earth hear the words of my mouth.

R.1: "Heavens, listen, and I will speak. \q Earth, hear what I have to say.

decisions.choice: heavens and earth called to listen, as witnesses
decisions.reason: Moses has said that he will call heaven and earth to witness against Israel (31:28; 4:26; 30:19). The song he was told to write and teach (31:19, 22, 30) begins by calling them to listen. Isaiah 1:2 opens in the same way.

decisions.choice: let me speak: Moses resolves to speak, and the words that follow are his song
decisions.reason: The verb expresses the speaker's intention. "The words of my mouth" are the song itself, which runs to verse 43.

decisions.choice: quotation marks open here and close at the end of verse 43
decisions.reason: The song is introduced at 31:30 as Moses speaking its words to the whole assembly, so it is set as one quotation. Words of God quoted inside it take single quotes.

records.heading: The song of Moses

records.source: יַעֲרֹ֤ף כַּמָּטָר֙ לִקְחִ֔י תִּזַּ֥ל כַּטַּ֖ל אִמְרָתִ֑י כִּשְׂעִירִ֣ם עֲלֵי־דֶ֔שֶׁא וְכִרְבִיבִ֖ים עֲלֵי־עֵֽשֶׂב׃
records.gloss: Let drop like the rain my teaching; let distill like the dew my speech, like showers on fresh grass, and like heavy rains on vegetation.
pieces: May my teaching fall like rain, \q my words settle like the dew, \q like soft rain on young grass, \q like showers on growing plants.

L.2: Let my teaching drop like the rain; \q let my speech distill like the dew, \q like gentle rains on fresh grass, \q and like showers on green plants.

R.2: Let my teaching come down like rain. \q Let my words fall gently like dew, \q like soft rain on new grass, \q like showers on young plants.

decisions.choice: teaching: what is handed on to be received and learned
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "take" and means instruction that a hearer takes in (Proverbs 4:2; Isaiah 29:24).

decisions.choice: two words for rain: light drizzle and heavy showers
decisions.reason: The first word is rare and is related to the word for hair, perhaps picturing fine drops; the second means abundant showers (Psalm 65:11; 72:6). Together with rain and dew they picture the song soaking into its hearers like water into a thirsty land.

decisions.choice: a wish: may my teaching come down
decisions.reason: The verbs express a wish rather than a prediction.

decisions.choice: my words
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means what is said, a saying; "my words" says it plainly.

records.source: כִּ֛י שֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֶקְרָ֑א הָב֥וּ גֹ֖דֶל לֵאלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: For [the] name of Yahweh I will proclaim; ascribe greatness to our God.
pieces: For I will proclaim the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q give our God the praise for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} greatness!

L.3: For I will proclaim the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q ascribe greatness to our God.

R.3: I will tell who {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is. \q Tell everyone how great our God is!

decisions.choice: for: the reason the heavens and earth should listen
decisions.reason: The word can also mean "when": "when I proclaim the name of the LORD, ascribe greatness to our God". Either way the song is about who the LORD is.

decisions.choice: proclaim the name: declare who the LORD is and what he has done
decisions.reason: God's name stands for his character, which he himself proclaimed to Moses (Exodus 33:19; 34:5-7).

decisions.choice: ascribe greatness: acknowledge that he is great
decisions.reason: The verb means "give"; giving greatness to God means confessing and praising it, as in Psalm 29:1-2. The command is plural, addressed to the hearers.

decisions.choice: tell who the LORD is
decisions.reason: Readable says what "proclaim the name" means.

records.source: הַצּוּר֙ תָּמִ֣ים פָּעֳל֔וֹ כִּ֥י כָל־דְּרָכָ֖יו מִשְׁפָּ֑ט אֵ֤ל אֱמוּנָה֙ וְאֵ֣ין עָ֔וֶל צַדִּ֥יק וְיָשָׁ֖ר הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: The Rock, perfect [is] his work, for all his ways [are] justice; a God of faithfulness and without injustice, righteous and upright [is] he.
pieces: The Rock: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work is perfect, \q and all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways are just. \q A faithful God who does no wrong, \q righteous and upright is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}.

L.4: The Rock: perfect [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work, \q for all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways [are] justice; \q a God of faithfulness and without injustice, \q righteous and upright [is] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}.

R.4: God is the Rock, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work is perfect. \q All {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways are just. \q He is a faithful God who does no wrong. \q He is righteous and honest.

decisions.choice: the Rock: a title of God, the one who is firm, strong and a safe refuge
decisions.reason: The Rock is the song's key name for God (verses 4, 15, 18, 30, 31). A great rock is a place of shelter and a picture of what cannot be moved (Psalm 18:3; Isaiah 26:4). The song sets this Rock against the false "rock" of other peoples (verses 31, 37).

decisions.choice: perfect: complete, without flaw
decisions.reason: The same word describes an animal fit for sacrifice and a person of integrity (Genesis 6:9). It contrasts with the "defect" of his people in verse 5.

decisions.choice: a God of faithfulness: one who is reliable and keeps his word
decisions.reason: The word means firmness and trustworthiness. "Without injustice" says the same thing from the other side: he never does wrong.

decisions.choice: Rock, with a capital letter, as a title of God
decisions.reason: Where the word is a name for God it is written "Rock" at every level. Where it means stone (verse 13) or the gods of other nations (verses 31, 37) it is written "rock".

decisions.choice: God is the Rock
decisions.reason: Readable makes a full sentence of the title that opens the verse.

records.source: שִׁחֵ֥ת ל֛וֹ לֹ֖א בָּנָ֣יו מוּמָ֑ם דּ֥וֹר עִקֵּ֖שׁ וּפְתַלְתֹּֽל׃
records.gloss: It has acted corruptly toward him, not his children, their defect; a generation crooked and twisted.
pieces: They have acted corruptly toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; by their own fault they are not {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children, \q a twisted and crooked generation.

L.5: They have acted corruptly toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; [they are] not {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children, [it is] their defect; \q a generation crooked and twisted.

R.5: His people have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Because of their faults, they are not {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children. \q They are twisted and dishonest people.

decisions.choice: they acted corruptly toward him; by their defect they are not his children
alternatives: their defect is not his children's
they have dealt corruptly with him, his no-children
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this line is very compressed: a singular verb with no clear subject, then "not his children, their defect". It can be read "their defect is not that of his children" (the fault is theirs, not his), or "they are not his children, because of their defect", or, dividing the words differently, "his children who are not [his] have dealt corruptly". The Greek translation has "they sinned, not his children, blemished ones". All readings agree that the people, not God, are to blame. Reviewers check this against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: defect: a blemish that disqualifies
decisions.reason: The word is used for the blemish that keeps an animal from being offered (Leviticus 22:20; Deuteronomy 15:21; 17:1). It stands against the "perfect" work of the Rock in verse 4.

decisions.choice: a crooked and twisted generation
decisions.reason: The phrase is taken up in Philippians 2:15. The words picture something bent out of the straight path, the opposite of the "upright" God of verse 4.

decisions.choice: they, for the singular verb
decisions.reason: The subject is the people as a whole, so English uses "they".

records.source: הֲ־לַיְהוָה֙ תִּגְמְלוּ־זֹ֔את עַ֥ם נָבָ֖ל וְלֹ֣א חָכָ֑ם הֲלוֹא־הוּא֙ אָבִ֣יךָ קָּנֶ֔ךָ ה֥וּא עָֽשְׂךָ֖ וַֽיְכֹנְנֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: ? To Yahweh do you repay this, people foolish and not wise? ? Not he [is] your father [who] created you, he made you and established you?
pieces: Is this how you repay {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q you foolish and senseless people? \q Is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not your father, who brought you into being, \q who made you and set you firmly in place?

L.6: Is this how you repay {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q people foolish and not wise? \q Is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not your father, who created you, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who made you and established you?

R.6: Is this how you pay {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} back, \q you foolish people with no sense? \q He is your father who created you. \q He made you and formed you into a people.

decisions.choice: the question marker written as a large letter
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew manuscripts the first letter of this verse, the sign of a question, is written large and as a word on its own. It is a scribal mark that draws attention to the question; it does not change the meaning.

decisions.choice: created you: brought you into being as his own
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "create" (Genesis 14:19, 22) or "acquire, buy" (Exodus 15:16, "the people you acquired"). Both senses fit: he made Israel and made Israel his.

decisions.choice: your father: God as the one who gave Israel life and cares for it
decisions.reason: Israel is called God's son in Exodus 4:22 and Deuteronomy 1:31; 8:5; 14:1. The song returns to this picture in verse 18.

decisions.choice: foolish: morally senseless, not only lacking intelligence
decisions.reason: This kind of fool is one who disregards God (Psalm 14:1). The same word returns in verse 21.

decisions.choice: the second question as two statements
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "yes", so Readable states it.

decisions.choice: formed you into a people
decisions.reason: The verb means to set up firmly; Readable says what God made of Israel.

records.source: זְכֹר֙ יְמ֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם בִּ֖ינוּ שְׁנ֣וֹת דּוֹר־וָד֑וֹר שְׁאַ֤ל אָבִ֨יךָ֙ וְיַגֵּ֔דְךָ זְקֵנֶ֖יךָ וְיֹ֥אמְרוּ לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Remember [the] days of antiquity; consider [the] years of generation and generation; ask your father and he will tell you, your elders, and they will say to you.
pieces: Remember the days of long ago; \q think about the years of past generations. \q Ask your father, and he will tell you; \q ask your elders, and they will explain it to you.

L.7: Remember the days of old; \q consider the years of generation after generation; \q ask your father, and he will tell you, \q your elders, and they will say [it] to you.

R.7: Remember what happened long ago. \q Think about the years of many generations. \q Ask your father, and he will tell you. \q Ask your elders, and they will explain.

decisions.choice: commands to the people as one and as many
decisions.reason: "Remember" and "ask" are singular, "consider" is plural: the song addresses Israel both as one people and as its many members.

decisions.choice: the years of generation after generation: all the past ages
decisions.reason: Repeating "generation" means one generation after another.

decisions.choice: fathers and elders as those who pass on Israel's history
decisions.reason: Parents are to tell their children what God has done (4:9; 6:20-25). What they will tell follows in verses 8-14.

decisions.choice: ask (repeated)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves the verb to be understood with "your elders"; Balanced and Readable repeat it.

records.source: בְּהַנְחֵ֤ל עֶלְיוֹן֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם בְּהַפְרִיד֖וֹ בְּנֵ֣י אָדָ֑ם יַצֵּב֙ גְּבֻלֹ֣ת עַמִּ֔ים לְמִסְפַּ֖ר בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: When gave an inheritance [the] Most High [to the] nations, when he separated [the] sons of humankind, he set [the] boundaries of peoples according to [the] number of [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: When the Most High gave each nation its inheritance, \q when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} divided up humanity, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fixed the borders of the peoples \q according to the number of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.8: When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, \q when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} divided the {{gender:children|sons}} of humankind, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set the boundaries of the peoples \q according to the number of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.8: The Most High gave each nation its land. \q He divided up the human race. \q He set the borders of the peoples \q by the number of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: according to the number of the sons of Israel
alternatives: according to the number of the sons of God
according to the number of the angels of God
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew text reads "sons of Israel". A Hebrew manuscript of Deuteronomy found at Qumran reads "sons of God", and the Greek translation reads "angels of God" (some copies "sons of God"). On that reading the Most High set the nations under heavenly beings (compare 4:19; 29:25; Psalm 82; Daniel 10:13, 20), but kept Israel for himself (verse 9). On the Hebrew reading the borders of the nations were set with Israel in view; the seventy nations of Genesis 10 may match the seventy of Jacob's family who went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:27; Exodus 1:5). This text follows the standard Hebrew. Reviewers check this against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: the Most High: a title of God as ruler over all nations
decisions.reason: The title stresses that God stands above every people (Genesis 14:18-22; Psalm 47:3). In the song he is the God who takes Israel as his own share in verse 9.

decisions.choice: dividing humankind: the spread of the nations after the flood
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the nations separating in Genesis 10:5, 32, after the tower of Babel (Genesis 11:8-9). The "inheritance" of each nation is its land.

decisions.choice: gave each nation its land
decisions.reason: Readable says what the nations' "inheritance" was.

records.source: כִּ֛י חֵ֥לֶק יְהֹוָ֖ה עַמּ֑וֹ יַעֲקֹ֖ב חֶ֥בֶל נַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: For [the] portion of Yahweh [is] his people; Jacob [is the] measured allotment of his inheritance.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s own portion is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people; \q Jacob is the share {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} measured out as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} inheritance.

L.9: For the portion of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people; \q Jacob [is] the allotted share of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} inheritance.

R.9: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s own share is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. \q The descendants of Jacob belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the LORD kept Israel for himself, unlike the other nations
decisions.reason: The connecting word links this verse to verse 8 and can be read "for", "but" or "indeed". The nations received their lands; the LORD's own share was a people.

decisions.choice: allotted share: a portion measured out with a cord
decisions.reason: The word means a measuring line, and then the share of land it marks out (Joshua 17:5; Psalm 16:6).

decisions.choice: Jacob: the people descended from Jacob, Israel
decisions.reason: The ancestor's name stands for the nation, as often in poetry (33:10, 28).

decisions.choice: but
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "but" to show the contrast with the nations in verse 8; Literal keeps "for".

decisions.choice: the descendants of Jacob belong to him
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "the share of his inheritance" means.

records.source: יִמְצָאֵ֨הוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִדְבָּ֔ר וּבְתֹ֖הוּ יְלֵ֣ל יְשִׁמֹ֑ן יְסֹֽבְבֶ֨נְהוּ֙ יְב֣וֹנְנֵ֔הוּ יִצְּרֶ֖נְהוּ כְּאִישׁ֥וֹן עֵינֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: He found him in a land of wilderness, and in a waste of howling of desolation; he surrounded him, he cared for him, he guarded him like [the] pupil of his eye.
pieces: He found him in a desert land, \q in an empty waste where the wind howls. \q He shielded him on every side and watched over him; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} guarded him as the pupil of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eye.

L.10: He found him in a desert land, \q and in a howling waste of wilderness; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} surrounded him, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cared for him, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} guarded him like the pupil of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eye.

R.10: He found {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people in a desert land, \q in an empty waste where the wind howls. \q He surrounded them and took care of them. \q He protected them as carefully as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would protect {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own eye.

decisions.choice: he found him in the wilderness: God took up Israel in the desert
decisions.reason: The song pictures Israel as a lost person whom God found and rescued (Hosea 9:10; Jeremiah 2:2, 6). It recalls the forty years in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: howling: the howl of wind or of wild animals in the waste
decisions.reason: The word means a wailing sound. "Waste" is the word for the empty earth in Genesis 1:2.

decisions.choice: surrounded him, cared for him: protected him on every side and paid close attention to him
decisions.reason: The second verb comes from the word for understanding; it may mean "gave him attention" or "taught him".

decisions.choice: the pupil of his eye: what a person guards most carefully
decisions.reason: The word means "little man", the tiny figure reflected in the eye. The same picture is in Psalm 17:8 and Proverbs 7:2.

decisions.choice: his people, them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of Israel as "him"; Readable uses "his people" and "them" so the reader is not confused with God.

records.source: כְּנֶ֨שֶׁר֙ יָעִ֣יר קִנּ֔וֹ עַל־גּוֹזָלָ֖יו יְרַחֵ֑ף יִפְרֹ֤שׂ כְּנָפָיו֙ יִקָּחֵ֔הוּ יִשָּׂאֵ֖הוּ עַל־אֶבְרָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Like an eagle [that] stirs up its nest, over its young it hovers; it spreads its wings, it takes him, it carries him on its pinion,
pieces: Like an eagle that rouses its nest \q and hovers over its young, \q that spreads its wings to catch them \q and carries them on its feathers,

L.11: Like an eagle that stirs up its nest, \q that hovers over its young, \q it spreads its wings, takes them, \q carries them on its pinions,

R.11: God was like an eagle that stirs up its nest \q and flies over its young. \q It spreads its wings to catch them \q and carries them on its feathers.

decisions.choice: eagle: a great bird of prey, perhaps the griffon vulture
decisions.reason: The word covers the largest birds of prey. Exodus 19:4 uses the same picture: "I carried you on eagles' wings."

decisions.choice: stirs up its nest and hovers: teaching the young to fly and watching over them
decisions.reason: The picture seems to be of a parent bird that makes its young leave the nest and stays close to catch them. The verb "hovers" is the one used of God's Spirit over the waters in Genesis 1:2.

decisions.choice: takes him, carries him: the eagle's care pictures God's care for Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pronouns are singular, "him", where the young are plural, so the picture turns toward Israel, whom God carried. The sentence runs into verse 12: the LORD alone guided him.

decisions.choice: them, for the singular object
decisions.reason: English follows the eagle's young, so the verse reads clearly as one picture; verse 12 applies it to Israel.

decisions.choice: God was like
decisions.reason: Readable makes its own sentence of the comparison and says who is being compared.

records.source: יְהוָ֖ה בָּדָ֣ד יַנְחֶ֑נּוּ וְאֵ֥ין עִמּ֖וֹ אֵ֥ל נֵכָֽר׃
records.gloss: Yahweh alone guided him, and [there was] not with him a god of foreignness.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} alone led him; \q no foreign god was at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} side.

L.12: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} alone guided him, \q and [there was] no foreign god with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.12: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} led {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people all by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}. \q No foreign god helped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: alone: no other god had any part in Israel's rescue
decisions.reason: The song prepares for its claim in verse 39 that there is no god besides him (4:35, 39).

decisions.choice: with him: with the LORD
alternatives: there was no foreign god with Israel
decisions.reason: The words can also mean that no foreign god was with Israel at that time, before Israel turned to other gods (verses 16-17).

decisions.choice: helped him
decisions.reason: Readable says what being "with him" means here.

records.source: יַרְכִּבֵ֨הוּ֙ עַל־בָּ֣מֳתֵיאָ֔רֶץ וַיֹּאכַ֖ל תְּנוּבֹ֣ת שָׂדָ֑י וַיֵּנִקֵ֤הֽוּ דְבַשׁ֙ מִסֶּ֔לַע וְשֶׁ֖מֶן מֵחַלְמִ֥ישׁ צֽוּר׃
records.gloss: He made him ride on [the] high places of [the] land, and he ate [the] produce of [the] field; and he made him suck honey from [the] rock and oil from [the] flint of [the] rock,
pieces: He set him riding over the heights of the land, \q and he ate the crops of the fields. \q He fed him honey from the crags \q and oil from the hard rock,

L.13: He made him ride on the heights of the land, \q and he ate the produce of the field; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made him suck honey from the rock, \q and oil from the flinty rock,

R.13: He let {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people ride over the hills of the land \q and eat the crops of its fields. \q He gave them honey from the rocks \q and olive oil from stony ground.

decisions.choice: ride on the heights of the land: to hold the land in safety and triumph
decisions.reason: The same picture is used for Israel in 33:29 and Isaiah 58:14, and for God in Amos 4:13.

decisions.choice: honey from the rock, oil from flint: plenty even from the hardest ground
decisions.reason: Wild bees nest in rock crevices, and olive trees grow on rocky hillsides. The land gives food even where nothing seems able to grow (8:7-9).

decisions.choice: heights: the written form and the form read aloud differ slightly
decisions.reason: The Hebrew manuscripts write the word for "heights" one way and mark it to be read another; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: he ate: Israel ate
decisions.reason: The verb is singular; the subject is Israel. The Greek translation reads "he fed him".

decisions.choice: olive oil
decisions.reason: The oil is olive oil; Readable says so.

records.source: חֶמְאַ֨ת בָּקָ֜ר וַחֲלֵ֣ב צֹ֗אן עִם־חֵ֨לֶב כָּרִ֜ים וְאֵילִ֤ים בְּנֵֽי־בָשָׁן֙ וְעַתּוּדִ֔ים עִם־חֵ֖לֶב כִּלְי֣וֹת חִטָּ֑ה וְדַם־עֵנָ֖ב תִּשְׁתֶּה־חָֽמֶר׃
records.gloss: curd[s] of [the] herd and milk of [the] flock, with [the] fat of lambs and rams, sons of Bashan, and he-goats, with [the] fat of [the] kidneys of wheat; and [the] blood of [the] grape you drank, wine.
pieces: curds from the cattle and milk from the flock, with the fat of lambs, and rams of Bashan, and goats, \q with the finest of the wheat; \q and you drank wine, the foaming blood of grapes.

L.14: curds of the herd and milk of the flock, with the fat of lambs, and rams, breed of Bashan, and goats, \q with the kidney fat of wheat; \q and the blood of the grape you drank, foaming wine.

R.14: He gave them cream and milk from their cattle and sheep, fat lambs and goats, fine rams from Bashan, \q and the best wheat. \q You drank rich red wine.

decisions.choice: rams of Bashan: of the breed of Bashan, the rich grazing land east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: "Sons of Bashan" means animals raised there. Bashan was famous for its herds (Amos 4:1; Ezekiel 39:18).

decisions.choice: the kidney fat of wheat: the very best wheat
decisions.reason: The fat around the kidneys was the richest part of an animal and was given to God (Leviticus 3:4). Fat stands for the best of anything (Numbers 18:12; Psalm 81:17; 147:14).

decisions.choice: the blood of the grape: red wine
decisions.reason: The same picture is in Genesis 49:11. The word for wine here may mean foaming or fermenting wine.

decisions.choice: you drank: the song turns to address Israel directly
decisions.reason: The list continues the gifts of verse 13, then speaks to Israel as "you".

decisions.choice: cream
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means thickened or curdled milk; Readable uses a common word.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ן יְשֻׁרוּן֙ וַיִּבְעָ֔ט שָׁמַ֖נְתָּ עָבִ֣יתָ כָּשִׂ֑יתָ וַיִּטֹּשׁ֙ אֱל֣וֹהַ עָשָׂ֔הוּ וַיְנַבֵּ֖ל צ֥וּר יְשֻׁעָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And grew fat Jeshurun and he kicked; you grew fat, you grew thick, you became gorged; and he abandoned God [who] made him, and he treated with contempt [the] Rock of his salvation.
pieces: But Jeshurun grew fat and kicked out; \q you grew fat, heavy and sleek. \q He abandoned the God who made him \q and treated the Rock of his salvation with contempt.

L.15: But Jeshurun grew fat and kicked; \q you grew fat, you grew thick, you were gorged; \q and he abandoned God who made him \q and scorned the Rock of his salvation.

R.15: But Israel grew fat and kicked like a stubborn animal. \q You grew fat, heavy and stuffed with food. \q They left the God who made them \q and rejected the Rock of their salvation.

decisions.choice: Jeshurun: a poetic name for Israel, meaning "the upright one"
decisions.reason: The name comes from the word for upright, used of God in verse 4, and is used for Israel again in 33:5, 26 and Isaiah 44:2. Here it is pointed: the "upright one" has turned crooked (verse 5).

decisions.choice: grew fat and kicked: like a well-fed animal that kicks against its owner
decisions.reason: Plenty made Israel stubborn instead of grateful, as Moses warned (6:10-12; 8:12-14; 31:20). The same picture of kicking is in 1 Samuel 2:29.

decisions.choice: you grew fat: the song turns to speak to Israel directly, then back to "he"
decisions.reason: The three verbs in the middle of the verse are addressed to "you". Such shifts between "he" and "you" are common in Hebrew poetry.

decisions.choice: the Rock of his salvation: the God who rescued him
decisions.reason: The title joins the song's name for God (verse 4) with what he did for Israel. To scorn him is to treat as worthless the one who saved them.

decisions.choice: Israel
decisions.reason: Readable writes "Israel" for Jeshurun, as the meaning decision explains, and "they" for the people.

decisions.choice: kicked like a stubborn animal
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of kicking means.

records.source: יַקְנִאֻ֖הוּ בְּזָרִ֑ים בְּתוֹעֵבֹ֖ת יַכְעִיסֻֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: They made him jealous with strange [ones]; with abominations they provoked him to anger.
pieces: They made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} jealous with foreign gods; \q with detestable things they made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} angry.

L.16: They made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} jealous with strange [gods]; \q with abominations they provoked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to anger.

R.16: They made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} jealous by worshiping other gods. \q They made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} angry with the disgusting things they did.

decisions.choice: strange ones: foreign gods
decisions.reason: The word means strangers, outsiders; here it is used of gods that do not belong to Israel (Jeremiah 2:25; 3:13).

decisions.choice: jealous: God's rightful claim to Israel's loyalty alone
decisions.reason: God is a jealous God, as a husband is jealous for his wife (5:9; Exodus 20:5; 34:14). The same verb returns in verse 21.

decisions.choice: abominations: practices God detests, especially the worship of idols
decisions.reason: The word is used for idols and the rites that go with them (7:25-26; 12:31; 13:15).

decisions.choice: gods
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "strange ones"; English supplies "gods" (in brackets at Literal).

records.source: יִזְבְּח֗וּ לַשֵּׁדִים֙ לֹ֣א אֱלֹ֔הַ אֱלֹהִ֖ים לֹ֣א יְדָע֑וּם חֲדָשִׁים֙ מִקָּרֹ֣ב בָּ֔אוּ לֹ֥א שְׂעָר֖וּם אֲבֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: They sacrificed to the demons, not God, gods [whom] they had not known, new [ones who] from nearby came, [whom] your fathers did not dread.
pieces: They sacrificed to demons that were not God, \q to gods they had never known, \q new gods who had recently arrived, \q whom your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} never feared.

L.17: They sacrificed to demons, not God, \q to gods they had not known, \q new [gods] who came lately, \q whom your fathers did not dread.

R.17: They offered sacrifices to demons, which are not God, \q to gods they had never known before. \q These were new gods that had just come along, \q gods your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} never feared.

decisions.choice: demons: spirit beings other than God
decisions.reason: The word is used only here and in Psalm 106:37, both times for spirits to whom people sacrificed. A related word names protective spirits in the religions of Mesopotamia. Paul takes up this verse in 1 Corinthians 10:20.

decisions.choice: not God: beings that are not God
alternatives: to demons, and not to God
decisions.reason: The phrase can also be read "they sacrificed to demons and not to God". Either way the point is that their worship went to what is not God (verse 21).

decisions.choice: did not dread: did not stand in awe of them
decisions.reason: The verb is rare. It seems to mean to shudder or bristle with awe; some relate it to a word meaning "know", "whom your fathers did not know".

decisions.choice: new ones who came lately: gods of recent arrival
decisions.reason: The words stress how new and untried these gods were, in contrast to the God of the "days of old" (verse 7).

decisions.choice: ancestors, with fathers as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means the forebears of the whole people.

records.source: צ֥וּר יְלָדְךָ֖ תֶּ֑שִׁי וַתִּשְׁכַּ֖ח אֵ֥ל מְחֹלְלֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: [The] Rock [who] fathered you you neglected, and you forgot God [who] brought you forth in birth.
pieces: You neglected the Rock who fathered you; \q you forgot the God who gave you birth.

L.18: The Rock who fathered you, you neglected, \q and you forgot God who gave you birth.

R.18: You forgot the Rock who was your father. \q You forgot the God who gave birth to you.

decisions.choice: fathered you, gave you birth: God pictured as both father and mother
decisions.reason: The first verb can be used of a father or a mother; the second describes a woman in labor. The song uses both to say how closely Israel's life came from God (verse 6; Isaiah 42:14; 49:15).

decisions.choice: neglected: forgot, disregarded
decisions.reason: The verb is rare and parallels "forgot". In the Hebrew manuscripts one of its letters is written small, a scribal mark that does not change the meaning.

decisions.choice: forgot (twice)
decisions.reason: Readable uses one common word for the two Hebrew verbs.

records.source: וַיַּ֥רְא יְהוָ֖ה וַיִּנְאָ֑ץ מִכַּ֥עַס בָּנָ֖יו וּבְנֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And saw Yahweh and he spurned [them], because of [the] provocation of his sons and his daughters.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} saw it and rejected them, \q because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sons and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} daughters provoked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.19: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spurned [them], \q because of the provocation of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sons and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} daughters.

R.19: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} saw this and turned away from them, \q because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sons and daughters had made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} angry.

decisions.choice: spurned: rejected with contempt
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat with scorn (Numbers 14:11, 23; Jeremiah 14:21). Israel scorned the Rock (verse 15); now God rejects them.

decisions.choice: because of the provocation of his sons and daughters: because they provoked him
decisions.reason: The phrase gives the cause: what his children did stirred his anger. It may also mean he spurned them in his anger at them.

decisions.choice: sons and daughters: the whole people, men and women
decisions.reason: Naming both makes clear that all of Israel is meant. They are still called his children.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַסְתִּ֤ירָה פָנַי֙ מֵהֶ֔ם אֶרְאֶ֖ה מָ֣ה אַחֲרִיתָ֑ם כִּ֣י ד֤וֹר תַּהְפֻּכֹת֙ הֵ֔מָּה בָּנִ֖ים לֹא־אֵמֻ֥ן בָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And he said, I will hide my face from them; I will see what [will be] their end; for a generation of perversities [are] they, children [in] whom [there is] not faithfulness.
pieces: He said, 'I will hide {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face from them \q and see what their end will be, \q for they are a perverse generation, \q children who cannot be trusted.

L.20: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, 'I will hide {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face from them; \q I will see what their end [will be]; \q for they [are] a generation of perversity, \q children in whom [there is] no faithfulness.

R.20: He said, 'I will turn away from them. \q I will see what happens to them in the end. \q They are a twisted generation, \q children who are not loyal to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: God himself speaks from here
decisions.reason: The song now gives God's own words, in the first person, through verse 27. Verses 34-35 and 37-42 are his words again.

decisions.choice: hide my face: withdraw favor, help and protection
decisions.reason: God warned of this in 31:17-18. It is the opposite of the blessing "may the LORD make his face shine on you" (Numbers 6:25; Psalm 13:2).

decisions.choice: faithfulness: loyalty, trustworthiness
decisions.reason: The word is related to "faithful" in verse 4. God is faithful; his children are not.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks from here to the end of verse 27
decisions.reason: God's words are a quotation inside Moses' song, so they take single quotes.

decisions.choice: turn away from them
decisions.reason: Readable says what hiding the face means.

records.source: הֵ֚ם קִנְא֣וּנִי בְלֹא־אֵ֔ל כִּעֲס֖וּנִי בְּהַבְלֵיהֶ֑ם וַאֲנִי֙ אַקְנִיאֵ֣ם בְּלֹא־עָ֔ם בְּג֥וֹי נָבָ֖ל אַכְעִיסֵֽם׃
records.gloss: They made me jealous with not-god; they provoked me with their vanities; and I will make them jealous with not-people; with a nation foolish I will provoke them.
pieces: They made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} jealous with what is no god \q and angered {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with their worthless idols; \q so I will make them jealous with those who are no people \q and anger them with a foolish nation.

L.21: They made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} jealous with a no-god; \q they provoked {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with their worthless idols; \q so I will make them jealous with a no-people; \q with a foolish nation I will provoke them.

R.21: They made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} jealous with things that are not gods. \q They made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry with their useless idols. \q So I will make them jealous with people who are not a real nation. \q I will make them angry with a foolish nation.

decisions.choice: no-god, no-people: God answers them in kind
decisions.reason: Israel gave its love to what is not a god; God will stir Israel's jealousy through a people that does not count as a people. Hosea 1:9-10 and 2:25 play on "not my people" in a similar way.

decisions.choice: worthless idols: things as empty as a breath
decisions.reason: The word means vapor or breath, and is used for idols that have no power (Jeremiah 8:19; 10:15).

decisions.choice: quoted in Romans 10:19
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the second half of this verse of the Gentiles, whose faith would move Israel to jealousy.

decisions.choice: a foolish nation: a people without understanding
decisions.reason: The word is the one used of Israel itself in verse 6; the nation God uses against Israel is no wiser than Israel.

records.source: כִּי־אֵשׁ֙ קָדְחָ֣ה בְאַפִּ֔י וַתִּיקַ֖ד עַד־שְׁא֣וֹל תַּחְתִּ֑ית וַתֹּ֤אכַל אֶ֨רֶץ֙ וִֽיבֻלָ֔הּ וַתְּלַהֵ֖ט מוֹסְדֵ֥י הָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: For a fire has been kindled in my anger, and it burns to Sheol, [the] lowest; and it devours [the] earth and its produce, and it sets ablaze [the] foundations of [the] mountains.
pieces: For a fire is kindled by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger; \q it burns down to the depths of Sheol. \q It consumes the earth and its crops \q and sets the roots of the mountains on fire.

L.22: For a fire has been kindled by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger, \q and it burns to the lowest Sheol; \q it devours the earth and its produce \q and sets ablaze the foundations of the mountains.

R.22: My anger has started a fire \q that burns down to the deepest part of the grave. \q It burns up the earth and its crops. \q It sets the foundations of the mountains on fire.

decisions.choice: the lowest Sheol: the deepest place of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place of the dead, pictured as under the earth (Numbers 16:30, 33; Psalm 86:13). The fire reaches from the depths below to the roots of the mountains: nothing is out of its reach.

decisions.choice: a fire kindled by my anger
decisions.reason: God's anger is pictured as fire (4:24; 29:19). Jeremiah 15:14 and 17:4 repeat this line.

decisions.choice: the foundations of the mountains: the deepest base of the world
decisions.reason: The mountains were thought of as resting on foundations deep in the earth (Psalm 18:8; Jonah 2:7).

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: Readable says "the grave" for Sheol; Literal and Balanced keep the name.

records.source: אַסְפֶּ֥ה עָלֵ֖ימוֹ רָע֑וֹת חִצַּ֖י אֲכַלֶּה־בָּֽם׃
records.gloss: I will heap upon them evils; my arrows I will use up against them.
pieces: I will pile disasters on them \q and spend {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arrows against them.

L.23: I will heap disasters on them; \q {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arrows I will use up against them.

R.23: I will pile troubles on them. \q I will shoot all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arrows at them.

decisions.choice: heap: gather and pile up
alternatives: I will add disasters to them
I will sweep disasters upon them
decisions.reason: The verb as written is usually "sweep away"; with slightly different vowels it means "add". The sense here is that God will add disaster upon disaster.

decisions.choice: my arrows: the disasters God sends
decisions.reason: God's arrows are the hunger, plague and beasts listed in verse 24 (Ezekiel 5:16; Psalm 38:3).

records.source: מְזֵ֥י רָעָ֛ב וּלְחֻ֥מֵי רֶ֖שֶׁף וְקֶ֣טֶב מְרִירִ֑י וְשֶׁן־בְּהֵמוֹת֙ אֲשַׁלַּח־בָּ֔ם עִם־חֲמַ֖ת זֹחֲלֵ֥י עָפָֽר׃
records.gloss: Weakened of famine and eaten of plague, and destruction bitter; and [the] tooth of beasts I will send against them, with [the] venom of crawlers of [the] dust.
pieces: They will waste away from hunger, devoured by plague and deadly disease. \q Against them I will send the teeth of wild animals, \q and the venom of snakes that glide in the dust.

L.24: [They will be] wasted by hunger, consumed by plague and bitter destruction; \q and the teeth of beasts I will send against them, \q with the venom of things crawling in the dust.

R.24: They will starve, and terrible sickness will destroy them. \q I will send wild animals to bite them \q and poisonous snakes to strike them.

decisions.choice: plague: burning fever or pestilence
decisions.reason: The word means a flame or a fiery disease. It is also the name of a Canaanite god of plague; Habakkuk 3:5 pictures plague going out before God as his servant.

decisions.choice: bitter destruction: deadly disease
decisions.reason: The word means a destroying sting or pestilence (Psalm 91:6; Isaiah 28:2).

decisions.choice: things crawling in the dust: snakes
decisions.reason: The phrase describes snakes (Micah 7:17; Genesis 3:14).

decisions.choice: hunger, plague and beasts: the punishments of the covenant
decisions.reason: The same troubles are named as covenant curses in Leviticus 26:22, 25-26 and Deuteronomy 28:21-22.

decisions.choice: wild animals to bite them, poisonous snakes to strike them
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain what the teeth and venom are.

records.source: מִחוּץ֙ תְּשַׁכֶּל־חֶ֔רֶב וּמֵחֲדָרִ֖ים אֵימָ֑ה גַּם־בָּחוּר֙ גַּם־בְּתוּלָ֔ה יוֹנֵ֖ק עִם־אִ֥ישׁ שֵׂיבָֽה׃
records.gloss: From outside will bereave a sword, and from inner rooms terror, both young man and young woman, nursing child with man of gray hair.
pieces: In the streets the sword will take their children, \q and inside their homes terror will strike, \q young men and young women alike, \q the nursing baby and the gray-haired.

L.25: Outside the sword will bereave, \q and in the inner rooms [will be] terror, \q both young man and young woman, \q the nursing child with the man of gray hair.

R.25: Outside, people will be killed in battle. \q Inside their houses, people will be terrified. \q Young men and young women will die, \q and so will babies and old people.

decisions.choice: the sword will bereave: war will kill their children
decisions.reason: The verb means to make childless (Leviticus 26:22; Lamentations 1:20).

decisions.choice: outside and in the inner rooms: everywhere
decisions.reason: There will be no safe place: the sword in the streets and terror in the most private rooms of the house.

decisions.choice: young man and young woman, infant and gray-haired: everyone, of every age
decisions.reason: Pairing opposites names the whole population.

decisions.choice: will die
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sword will do to each group.

records.source: אָמַ֖רְתִּי אַפְאֵיהֶ֑ם אַשְׁבִּ֥יתָה מֵאֱנ֖וֹשׁ זִכְרָֽם׃
records.gloss: I said, I will cut them in pieces; I will make cease from humankind their memory,
pieces: I would have said, "I will scatter them \q and wipe out their memory from among humankind,"

L.26: I said, "I will cut them in pieces; \q I will make their memory cease from humankind,"

R.26: I would have said, "I will scatter them far away. \q I will make sure no one remembers them."

decisions.choice: I said: I would have said, I would have decided
decisions.reason: God tells what he would have done, but verse 27 says why he held back.

decisions.choice: cut them in pieces: destroy them completely, perhaps by scattering them
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here. It may come from the word for a corner or edge, "I will drive them into the corners"; the Greek translation has "I will scatter them".

decisions.choice: make their memory cease: wipe them out so that no one remembers them
decisions.reason: The same is said of Amalek (25:19; Exodus 17:14).

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for God's words to himself inside his speech
decisions.reason: God's speech is already in single quotes inside Moses' song, so words he quotes take double quotes.

records.source: לוּלֵ֗י כַּ֤עַס אוֹיֵב֙ אָג֔וּר פֶּֽן־יְנַכְּר֖וּ צָרֵ֑ימוֹ פֶּן־יֹֽאמְרוּ֙ יָדֵ֣ינוּ רָ֔מָה וְלֹ֥א יְהוָ֖ה פָּעַ֥ל כָּל־זֹֽאת׃
records.gloss: if not [the] provocation of an enemy I dreaded, lest misconstrue their adversaries, lest they say, Our hand [is] raised, and not Yahweh did all this.
pieces: but I feared the taunting of the enemy, \q that their foes would misunderstand \q and say, "Our own power has won; \q it was not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who did all this."'

L.27: had I not feared the provocation of the enemy, \q lest their adversaries misunderstand, \q lest they say, "Our hand [is] raised high, \q and [it was] not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [who] did all this."'

R.27: But I did not want their enemies to boast. \q I did not want them to misunderstand and say, \q "We won by our own strength. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} did not do this."'

decisions.choice: the provocation of the enemy: the enemy's taunting that would provoke God
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for Israel provoking God in verses 16, 19 and 21; now it is what the enemy would do.

decisions.choice: our hand is raised high: we won by our own power
decisions.reason: A raised hand is a picture of strength and victory (Exodus 14:8; Numbers 33:3; Micah 5:8).

decisions.choice: God's concern that the nations see his hand
decisions.reason: Moses pleaded the same way, that the nations would misread God's acts (9:28; Exodus 32:12; Numbers 14:13-16). God holds back for his own name's sake.

decisions.choice: misunderstand: misread who did it
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat as foreign, to misconstrue; the enemies would take the credit.

decisions.choice: the single quotation mark closes God's speech here
decisions.reason: God's words that began in verse 20 end with this verse. Who speaks in verses 28-33 is open (see verse 28).

records.source: כִּי־ג֛וֹי אֹבַ֥ד עֵצ֖וֹת הֵ֑מָּה וְאֵ֥ין בָּהֶ֖ם תְּבוּנָֽה׃
records.gloss: For a nation lost of counsels [are] they, and there is not in them understanding.
pieces: For they are a nation without sense, \q and there is no understanding in them.

L.28: For they [are] a nation lost of counsel, \q and [there is] no understanding in them.

R.28: Those enemies are a nation with no sense. \q They do not understand anything.

decisions.choice: they: the enemy nation of verse 27
decisions.reason: Verses 28-33 most likely describe Israel's enemies, who would claim the victory as their own (verse 27) and whose "rock" and "vine" are not like Israel's (verses 31-32). decisions.reason: The word is not spite but the act of a ruler who punishes wrong and defends those wronged (verses 41, 43).

decisions.reason: A slipping foot is a picture of sudden downfall (Psalm 38:17; 94:18).

decisions.choice: what is prepared for them: the doom that awaits them
decisions.reason: The word means things that are ready, the future that is in store.

decisions.reason: Here judging means taking his people's side and setting things right (Psalm 135:14, which repeats this line; Genesis 30:6). Hebrews 10:30 quotes the line as a warning that God will judge his people.

decisions.reason: The verb means to be moved to pity and so to relent.

decisions.choice: their strength is gone, none left, bound or free: they are utterly helpless
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for strength. "Bound or free" pairs opposites to mean everyone, whatever their state (1 Kings 14:10; 2 Kings 14:26); its exact sense is uncertain, perhaps "under restraint or at liberty".

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: As with Moses "the slave of the LORD", Literal keeps the hard sense of the word; Balanced and Readable say "servants".

decisions.choice: do justice for
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the sense of "judge" here; Literal keeps "judge".

decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power, as in verse 36.

decisions.choice: I am the one true God

decisions.choice: the shorter text of the standard Hebrew
alternatives: Rejoice, heavens, with him; bow down to him, all gods
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew has four lines. A Hebrew manuscript from Qumran has six, beginning "Rejoice, heavens, with him, and bow down to him, all gods" and adding "and he will repay those who hate him". The Greek translation is longer still, with lines calling the sons of God and the angels of God to worship him. Hebrews 1:6 quotes a line close to the Greek ("let all God's angels worship him"), and Romans 15:10 quotes "Rejoice, nations, with his people". This text follows the standard Hebrew. Reviewers check this against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: shout for joy, nations, with his people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets "nations" and "his people" side by side with no word between them. It may mean "rejoice, nations, with his people" (as the Greek and Romans 15:10 have it), "nations, praise his people", or "rejoice, nations; rejoice, his people".

decisions.choice: make atonement for his land, his people: cleanse the land and people from the guilt of bloodshed
decisions.reason: Blood shed on the land defiles it, and atonement cleanses it (21:1-9; Numbers 35:33). The Qumran manuscript, the Samaritan Pentateuch and the Greek read "the land of his people".

decisions.choice: he will avenge the blood of his servants: God will set right the wrong done to his people
decisions.reason: The song ends not with destruction but with God defending his people and cleansing his land (verses 35-36, 39).

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: As in verse 36.

decisions.choice: the double quotation mark closes the song
decisions.reason: The song that opened at verse 1 ends here.

records.gloss: And came Moses and spoke all [the] words of the song the this in [the] ears of the people, he and Hoshea son of Nun.
pieces: Moses, together with Joshua son of Nun, came and recited the whole song for the people to hear.

L.44: And Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people, he and Hoshea son of Nun.

R.44: Moses and Joshua son of Nun came and spoke all the words of this song so that the people could hear them.

decisions.choice: Hoshea: Joshua's earlier name
decisions.reason: Hoshea was Joshua's name until Moses called him Joshua (Numbers 13:8, 16). Only here is the old name used after that. The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Greek translation read "Joshua".

decisions.choice: in the ears of the people: so that the people heard
decisions.reason: Moses did what God told him: write the song and teach it to Israel (31:19, 22, 30).

decisions.choice: he and Joshua: Moses and his successor together
decisions.reason: Joshua had just been commissioned to lead the people after Moses (31:7-8, 14, 23).

decisions.choice: Joshua
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the name the reader knows; Literal keeps "Hoshea" as the Hebrew has it.

records.heading: It is your very life

records.source: וַיְכַ֣ל מֹשֶׁ֗ה לְדַבֵּ֛ר אֶת־כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה אֶל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And finished Moses to speak all the words the these to all Israel,
pieces: When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,

L.45: And Moses finished speaking all these words to all Israel,

R.45: When Moses had finished saying all these words to all the people of Israel,

decisions.choice: all these words: the song, and with it the teaching Moses had given
decisions.reason: The words point back to the song just recited; the same phrase closes the writing of the law in 31:24.

decisions.choice: when ... had finished
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 46, so Balanced and Readable make this a time clause.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ שִׂ֣ימוּ לְבַבְכֶ֔ם לְכָל־הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י מֵעִ֥יד בָּכֶ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר תְּצַוֻּם֙ אֶת־בְּנֵיכֶ֔ם לִשְׁמֹ֣ר לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת אֶת־כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֖י הַתּוֹרָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: and he said to them, Set your heart to all the words which I [am] warning you the day, that you command them [to] your children, to keep to do all [the] words of the law the this.
pieces: he said to them, "Take to heart all the words I am solemnly declaring to you today, so that you may command your children to be careful to do all the words of this law.

L.46: and he said to them, "Set your heart on all the words that I am testifying to you today, which you shall command your children, to be careful to do all the words of this law.

R.46: he said to them, "Think carefully about all the words I have warned you with today. Command your children to obey carefully every word of this teaching.

decisions.choice: set your heart on: give your whole attention to, take to heart
decisions.reason: The heart is the place of thought and will; to set it on something is to fix the mind on it.

decisions.choice: testifying: solemnly warning, bearing witness
decisions.reason: The verb is used for calling witnesses and for solemn warning (4:26; 30:19; 31:28). The song itself is to be a witness (31:19, 21).

decisions.choice: this law: the whole of Moses' teaching
decisions.reason: As at 1:5, the word means instruction, everything Moses taught, not only rules.

decisions.choice: teaching
decisions.reason: Readable says "teaching" for the word Literal and Balanced render "law".

decisions.choice: quotation marks open here and close at the end of verse 47
decisions.reason: Moses' words to the people are a quotation inside the narrative.

records.gloss: For not a word empty [is] it from you, for it [is] your life, and by the word the this you will prolong days on the land which you [are] crossing the Jordan there to possess it.
pieces: It is no empty word for you; it is your very life. By this word you will live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess."

L.47: For it [is] not an empty word for you, for it [is] your life; and by this word you will prolong [your] days in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to take possession of [it]."

R.47: These are not just empty words. They are your life! By obeying them you will live a long time in the land across the Jordan River that you are going to take."

decisions.choice: an empty word: a thing of no account, without effect
decisions.reason: The word means empty or worthless. The teaching is not a matter that can be set aside without consequence; compare 30:11-14, where the command is not too hard or far away.

decisions.choice: it is your life: obeying the teaching is the way of life
decisions.reason: Moses has set before Israel life and death (30:15-20; 8:3).

decisions.choice: prolong days: live long
decisions.reason: The same promise is attached to obedience in 4:40; 5:33; 11:9.

decisions.choice: by obeying them
decisions.reason: Readable says how the word gives long life: by being obeyed.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה בְּעֶ֛צֶם הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses on [the] bone of the day the this, saying,
pieces: On that very day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

L.48: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses on that very day, saying,

R.48: That same day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: on the bone of this day: on that very day
decisions.reason: "Bone" here means the very substance of the day (Genesis 7:13; 17:23; Exodus 12:17). It is the day the song was taught.

decisions.choice: the LORD's word to Moses about his death
decisions.reason: God said the same in Numbers 27:12-14; now the time has come.

records.heading: Moses to die on Mount Nebo

records.source: עֲלֵ֡ה אֶל־הַר֩ הָעֲבָרִ֨ים הַזֶּ֜ה הַר־נְב֗וֹ אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֣י יְרֵח֑וֹ וּרְאֵה֙ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲנִ֥י נֹתֵ֛ן לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַאֲחֻזָּֽה׃
records.gloss: Go up to mountain the Abarim the this, Mount Nebo, which [is] in [the] land of Moab, which [is] on [the] face of Jericho, and see [the] land of Canaan which I [am] giving to [the] sons of Israel as a possession.
pieces: "Climb Mount Nebo here in the Abarim range, in the land of Moab, facing Jericho, and look out over the land of Canaan, which I am giving the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to possess.

L.49: "Go up into this mountain of the Abarim, Mount Nebo, which [is] in the land of Moab, which [is] opposite Jericho, and see the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel as a possession.

R.49: "Climb Mount Nebo in the Abarim mountains. It is in the land of Moab, facing Jericho. Look at the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to be their own.

decisions.choice: the Abarim mountains and Mount Nebo
decisions.reason: The Abarim are the highlands of Moab east of the Dead Sea and the Jordan; Nebo is one of their peaks, from which the land west of the Jordan can be seen (Numbers 27:12; 33:47-48; 34:1).

decisions.choice: opposite Jericho: facing Jericho across the Jordan
decisions.reason: Jericho lay west of the river, in view of Nebo.

decisions.choice: possession: land held as a permanent property
decisions.reason: The word is used for land held by a family or people (Genesis 17:8; Leviticus 25:24).

decisions.choice: quotation marks open here and close at the end of verse 52
decisions.reason: The LORD's words to Moses are a quotation inside the narrative.

records.source: וּמֻ֗ת בָּהָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ עֹלֶ֣ה שָׁ֔מָּה וְהֵאָסֵ֖ף אֶל־עַמֶּ֑יךָ כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־מֵ֞ת אַהֲרֹ֤ן אָחִ֨יךָ֙ בְּהֹ֣ר הָהָ֔ר וַיֵּאָ֖סֶף אֶל־עַמָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And die on the mountain which you [are] going up there, and be gathered to your people, just as died Aaron your brother on Hor the mountain and was gathered to his people,
pieces: On the mountain you climb you will die and be gathered to your people, just as Aaron your brother, who died on Mount Hor, was gathered to his people,

L.50: And die on the mountain that you are going up, and be gathered to your people, just as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people,

R.50: You will die on the mountain you climb, and you will join your people who died before you. That is what happened to your brother Aaron, who died on Mount Hor and joined his people.

decisions.choice: die and be gathered: an announcement of what will happen
decisions.reason: The verbs are commands in form, but they declare what God has decided (Numbers 27:13).

decisions.choice: be gathered to your people: die and join your ancestors who have died
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of Abraham, Jacob and Aaron (Genesis 25:8; 49:33; Numbers 20:24, 26).

decisions.choice: Aaron's death on Mount Hor
decisions.reason: Aaron died on Mount Hor on the border of Edom (Numbers 20:22-29; 33:38-39).

decisions.choice: you will die
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the command into the announcement it is; Literal keeps the command.

records.source: עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר מְעַלְתֶּ֜ם בִּ֗י בְּתוֹךְ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּמֵֽי־מְרִיבַ֥ת קָדֵ֖שׁ מִדְבַּר־צִ֑ן עַ֣ל אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־קִדַּשְׁתֶּם֙ אוֹתִ֔י בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: because that you broke faith with me in [the] midst of [the] sons of Israel at [the] waters of Meribah-kadesh, [the] wilderness of Zin, because that not you treated as holy me in [the] midst of [the] sons of Israel,
pieces: because both of you broke faith with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} at the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, and because you did not treat {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as holy among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.51: because you broke faith with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel at the waters of Meribah of Kadesh, [in the] wilderness of Zin, because you did not treat {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as holy among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.51: This is because you and Aaron were unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in front of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} at the waters of Meribah near Kadesh in the Zin Desert. You did not show them that I am holy.

decisions.choice: the waters of Meribah at Kadesh
decisions.reason: At Kadesh, when the people quarreled for lack of water, Moses struck the rock instead of speaking to it (Numbers 20:1-13; 27:14). "Meribah" means "quarreling".

decisions.choice: broke faith: acted unfaithfully, betrayed trust
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a serious breach of loyalty toward God (Leviticus 5:15; 26:40).

decisions.choice: did not treat me as holy: did not honor God's holiness before the people
decisions.reason: By not trusting and obeying God's word they failed to show the people how holy he is (Numbers 20:12).

decisions.choice: you: Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: The verbs are plural; both brothers are meant (Numbers 20:12, 24).

decisions.choice: both of you; you and Aaron
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that "you" is plural.

records.source: כִּ֥י מִנֶּ֖גֶד תִּרְאֶ֣ה אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְשָׁ֨מָּה֙ לֹ֣א תָב֔וֹא אֶל־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֥י נֹתֵ֖ן לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: for from opposite you will see the land, and there you will not go, to the land which I [am] giving to [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: You will see the land from a distance, but you will not enter it, the land I am giving to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}."

L.52: For from a distance you will see the land, but you will not go there, into the land that I am giving to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel."

R.52: You will see the land from far away, but you will not go into the land that I am giving to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}."

decisions.choice: from a distance: from where you stand, facing it
decisions.reason: The word means in front of, opposite; Moses will see the land spread out before him (3:27; 34:1-4).

decisions.choice: you will not go there: Moses' exclusion from the land
decisions.reason: God had refused Moses' plea to cross over (1:37; 3:23-27). Chapter 34 tells how this was fulfilled.

decisions.choice: the quotation mark closes the LORD's words
decisions.reason: The LORD's speech that began in verse 49 ends here.
